_comment: COUPLING tier-2. TWO-WAY thermo-structural interaction through the generic `couple` path, same code on both halves. One backward-Euler step of linear coupled thermoelasticity: the thermal participant solves the energy equation including the T_ref*beta*d/dt tr(eps) term and imports the volumetric strain; the structural participant solves quasi-static elasticity with the thermal stress and imports the temperature change. Both occupy the WHOLE body and exchange volume fields on non-matching meshes — this is a field coupling, not a domain decomposition, so `couple`'s interface-conservation checks report themselves as not-run and the verification is: convergence with a relaxation that is actually needed (at delta~1.25 the un-relaxed iteration diverges), agreement with an un-split monolithic re-solve, and the two direction controls. The reverse direction is switched off THROUGH THE COUPLING GRAPH (`imports_from=[]`) and separately through the participant's own COUPLING switch, and the fixture checks the two routes agree. It also checks the reference solver itself first, by an identity that needs no reference values: in uniaxial strain the two-way solve at rho_c must equal the one-way solve at rho_c*(1+delta).

_mutation.note: Kill the reverse direction outright. RUN: killed, 3 checks — validation_not_empty, thermal_unresponsive, thermal_insensitive. `couple`'s own machinery catches this one before the direction control is reached, because a thermal participant with no reverse term is no longer a function of its imports at all. That is the machinery working, and it is also why the NEXT mutation matters: a reverse direction that is present but WRONG stays perfectly responsive.

Flip the SIGN of the mechanical -> thermal term: expanding the body would then heat it instead of cooling it. RUN at a real metal's coupling strength (delta ~ 0.012): killed by ONE check, and not the one a reader would expect. The coupling converged, both participants stayed responsive and sensitive, and the comparison against the monolithic re-solve came out at 4.1e-03 against a 5e-03 tolerance — it PASSED. The whole reverse-direction effect is 0.15% of the answer at that delta, so doubling it stays inside the discretisation gap between the coupled meshes and the reference. Only the difference-of-differences control saw it: the coupled two-way-minus-one-way difference came out 2.017 (i.e. 200%) away from the same difference between the two monolithic solves, because it points the wrong way. This is the mutation that justifies the control's existence — a monolithic comparison alone would have shipped a sign-flipped TSI.

Give the STRUCTURAL half a thermal stress modulus 25% away from the thermal half's. The coupled run stays internally consistent — it converges, both participants respond, both directions are active — because both halves are simply solving a different problem than the one the reference solves. RUN: killed, 5 checks — the strain comparison against the monolithic solve in BOTH the two-way and one-way runs, the quality_checks monolithic detector in both, and the reverse-direction size. Same silent-wrong shape as the conductivity mutation in the heat pairs.
